environment.label: Environment
environment.unknownExplanation: The gateway did not say which deployment it is. Nothing here should be treated as safe to change until it does.
environment.sourcedFromApi: Reported by the gateway this app is talking to, not by the build.

error.invalidCredentials: That username and password did not match. Check both and try again.
error.throttled: Too many attempts from here. Wait a moment and try again.
error.throttledFor: Too many attempts from here. Try again in {{seconds}} seconds.
error.lockedOut: This account is locked after too many failed attempts. It unlocks once the window passes, or sooner if somebody with the server clears it.
error.lockedOutFor: This account is locked after too many failed attempts. It unlocks in {{seconds}} seconds, or sooner if somebody with the server clears it.
error.notAvailable: This deployment cannot sign you in. Trying again will not help; the server needs configuring.
error.unknown: Signing in failed, and the server did not say why. Check that the backend is reachable and try again.

warning.body: Nothing has been touched for a while, so this session is about to end. Anything you do keeps it.

reauth.heading: Session ended
reauth.body: Signed in as {{name}}. Enter the password to carry on. Nothing behind this has been lost, including anything half typed.
reauth.signOut: Sign out and lose unsaved work

serverDown.heading: The server is not answering
serverDown.body: This back office cannot reach its backend. Nothing on your screen has been lost, and it comes back on its own as soon as the server does.
serverDown.doNotReload: Do not reload this page if you have unsaved work. Reloading is the one thing that throws it away.
serverDown.retriesLeft_one: Checking again on its own {{count}} more time.
serverDown.retriesLeft_other: Checking again on its own {{count}} more times.
serverDown.stopped: Automatic checking has stopped. Use the button when you think the server is back.

notFound.heading: There is no such screen
notFound.body: The address you asked for does not belong to anything in this back office. It may have been a link from an older version.

list.noMatch: Nothing matches the filter. There are rows here; the filter is hiding them.
list.blocked: Choose {{filters}} first. There is nothing to read until you do.

reference.missing: This points at {{id}}, which no longer exists.

delete.heading: Delete this row?
delete.body: {{name}} will be deleted. There is no undo, and anything pointing at it may stop working.

discard.heading: Leave without saving?
discard.body: This form has changes that have not been saved. Leaving now loses them.

error.missingAnyLocale: A name in at least one language is needed.
error.localeTooLong: The {{locale}} text must be at most {{max}} characters.
error.notAUrl: Write a full web address, starting with http:// or https://.
error.tooPrecise: This column keeps {{decimals}} decimals. Values are not rounded for you, because a rounded price is a different price.
error.notAnOption: Choose one of the offered values.
error.notFound: That row is not there. Somebody may have deleted it.
error.forbidden: This account is not allowed to do that.
error.conflict: That change conflicts with the current state. Read the row again and try once more.
error.validation: Some of the values were refused. The details are beside the fields.
error.unreachable: The gateway did not answer. Check that the backend is running.
error.unknown: That did not work, and the server did not say why.
error.notAnObject: Write a JSON object, in braces. A list or a bare value is not what this column holds.

supermarkets.name: Name
supermarkets.externalBrandKeyHelp: The chain's stable identity across discovery runs. It is what splits Carrefour from Carrefour Express, so change it only when that is what you mean.
supermarkets.defaultPriceScopeIdHelp: Set by the catalog service, not from here.

locations.priceScopeIdHelp: Which prices this shop uses. Leave it empty when you create the shop, and catalog gives the shop a scope of its own.
locations.label: Name
locations.postalCodeHelp: Changing this does not move the shop to another price scope. The two are separate, and the pricing stays where it is.
locations.postalCodeSourceHelp: Where the code came from. Guessed means it was taken from the nearest centroid and nobody has checked it. Empty means the shop has no code at all, which is deliberate: a wrong code is worse than none.
locations.externalRefHelp: The discovery provider’s own reference, such as node/1156230891. It changes when a shop is remapped, so it is not a reliable identity.
locations.note: Shops are read one chain at a time, because the gateway has no route that lists them all. Choose a chain to begin.

priceScopes.supermarketIdHelp: The chain this scope prices for. It is fixed once the scope exists.
priceScopes.kindHelp: How wide the scope is. A warehouse scope is one price shared by every shop that warehouse serves. A single shop scope covers one shop.
priceScopes.externalKeyHelp: The source’s own key for the scope, such as a warehouse number. Text and not a number: it arrives as 4661 and as mad3.
priceScopes.label: Label
priceScopes.labelHelp: A name for people to read. Harvested scopes have none, and are shown by their kind and source key instead.

items.name: Name
items.eanHelp: The only identifier that joins a product across chains. Unique across the catalog.
items.unitSizeHelp: Without it the unit says nothing: a liter is not a size.
items.productGroupIdHelp: What makes this product comparable with another. Empty is the ordinary state of a newly harvested product, and nothing is wrong with it.

productGroups.name: Name
productGroups.slugHelp: A stable handle for tooling and tests: lower case words separated by single dashes.
productGroups.referenceUnitHelp: The unit this group’s members are compared in.
productGroups.synonymsHelp: Other words a shopper may use for this group. One per line.

prices.priceScopeIdHelp: A price belongs to a scope and not to a shop. Every shop that prices against this scope shows this price.
prices.priceHelp: What the till charges for one pack. Leave it empty for a product priced per kilogram.
prices.unitPriceHelp: The source’s own price per reference unit. Type it in. It is never worked out from the price and the size, because the two disagree on about one product in forty.
prices.unitPriceLabelHelp: The source’s own words for the unit price, such as 100 ml, or lv for washing machine loads. Free text and not a unit.
prices.validFromHelp: Leave it empty for a price that applies from the moment it is added.
prices.validUntilHelp: For a price you know is temporary. Leave it empty for one that holds until a better source replaces it.
prices.availableHelp: Scope wide. Whether one particular shop has it is a separate answer, on that shop’s own row.
prices.sourceKindHelp: Where the shown price came from. A price you add is recorded as typed in here. It is protected for seven days against a source repeating what you overrode, and a source saying something new is shown at once.
prices.observedAtHelp: When the shown price was last observed by its source.
prices.staleHelp: Nothing currently eligible prices this product, so the newest price anybody gave is shown and flagged. Set by the server from the price policies.
prices.note: The price a shopper sees, chosen among every price a source gave. A price belongs to a price scope, not to a shop. Open a row to see the prices behind it, add one, or remove one.

history.noEffective: No price is shown for this product in this scope.
history.none: No source has priced this product in this scope.

remove.heading: Remove this price?
remove.body: The {{kind}} price of {{price}} is removed from the history, and the price shoppers see is worked out again from what is left. Add a new price afterwards to correct a typo.

scope.heading: This price applies to {{scope}}.
scope.noLocations: No shop prices against it yet.
scope.none: Choose a price scope. A price belongs to a scope, not to a shop.

pricePolicies.priorityHelp: Lower wins. A leaflet at 10 outranks a website crawl at 30 whenever both are eligible.
pricePolicies.maxAgeDaysHelp: How old a price of this source may be before it stops being eligible. Empty means it never ages out. Typed in prices have none on purpose: for a chain with no automated source they are the only truth.
pricePolicies.enabledHelp: Off removes this source from every read at once.
pricePolicies.note: How each source competes for the price a shopper sees. Six rows, one per source.
pricePolicies.formNote: Saving works out the shown price again for every product in the catalog, inside this request.

locationItems.positionInStoreHelp: Where the product sits, such as an aisle. Per shop, because a warehouse cannot answer it.
locationItems.availableHelp: Whether this shop carries the product. Unset means nobody has said, and the scope’s own answer stands, which is not the same as saying no. Read only here: it is written by whoever last observed it, so the row can record which of a person and a crawl said so.
locationItems.note: These rows are read one shop at a time, because an aisle is a fact about one shop. Choose a shop to begin.

absent.heading: The harvester does not run here
absent.body: It is switched off in production and in staging on purpose, so nothing is deployed to answer this. Runs happen on a development machine against the compose stack. Nothing is broken and there is nothing to retry.

down.heading: The harvester did not answer
down.body: Something should be listening in this environment and nothing replied. Check that the harvester service and its database are running.

blocked.service-off: Harvesting is switched off on this deployment. HARVEST_ENABLED is false, so no run can start. It is server configuration and cannot be changed from here.
blocked.chain-disabled: That chain is switched off. Turn it on under chain sources, which is application state rather than server configuration.
blocked.unknown: The run could not start, and the server did not say which switch stopped it.

switch.heading: What is allowed to happen
switch.lead: Two separate decisions, neither of them changed from here. They are shown because otherwise there is no way to tell a run that did nothing from a run that was never allowed to. Whether a chain may be fetched is a third decision, and it is on the chain sources screen.

what.deployed: Whether the service exists in this environment at all. Set in the Helm chart.
what.harvestEnabled: Whether a running service may start any run. Set in the service configuration.

from.chart: From the chart, which switches the harvester off in production and in staging.
from.reply: Something answered a request on this screen.
from.silence: Nothing answered a request on this screen.
from.refusal: The server refused to start a run and named this switch.
from.run: A run got far enough that this switch must have been on.
from.failure: A run failed and named this switch.
from.nothing: No route reports this, and nothing has been attempted that would reveal it.

start.heading: Start a run
start.attribution: A run's writes are recorded against the harvester service, not against you. Starting one is what is being recorded here.
start.alreadyRunning: A run is already in progress. Only one runs at a time, so wait for it or abort it first.
start.failed: The run did not start, and the server did not say why.
start.leaflet: A leaflet import starts from the document itself: the file says which chain printed it, what is on offer and when the prices apply. Drop it on the import screen.

run.aborting: Stopping. The run is flushing what it has already fetched, which is kept, and will finish shortly.
run.paused: This tab is in the background, so the screen has stopped asking. These numbers are from the last read, not from now. Bring the tab forward to carry on.
run.pollFailed: The last read failed. What is shown is from before that.

progress.label: Run progress
progress.unsized: The run does not know yet how much work it has.

warnings.heading: What was dropped, and why
warnings.lead: One line per decision this run made without asking. The extractor's own lost tiles are here too, so what it lost and what the import dropped read in one place.

queue.open: Work through the names this chain has queued

revert.heading: Delete what this run wrote?
revert.confirm: Delete the {{prices}} prices this run wrote. Prices another run wrote, and prices you typed in yourself, are kept. This cannot be undone.
revert.confirmLeaflet: Delete the {{prices}} prices this run wrote and {{queued}} rows waiting in the queue. Accepted and rejected names are kept. This cannot be undone.

reverted.done: This run's prices were deleted and every product they priced was worked out again from what is left. The run kept its status, because that is how the run ended and reverting it did not change that. The same document can be imported again.

places.heading: Discovered places
places.empty: Every discovered place has been decided.
places.why: Nothing in the catalog matched this: neither its OpenStreetMap reference nor the same brand nearby. It is being offered rather than created.
places.supermarketId: Chain identifier to file it under (optional)

near.heading: Others of the same brand nearby
near.none: Nothing else of this brand is near it in the queue.

entries.heading: Source entries
entries.empty: Every entry for this chain has a catalog item.
entries.categoryHelp: The one thing the source does not tell us. Everything else on the item comes from the entry.

choose.body: Entries belong to one chain, so choose which chain to work through. The queue reads that chain's entries that have no catalog item yet.

correct.heading: Point it somewhere else
correct.help: If the match is wrong, give the source's own identifier for the right product. That replaces the link rather than removing it, so the item keeps a price.

sources.heading: Chain sources
sources.lead: How each chain is fetched, and whether it is fetched at all. This switch is per chain and is the one on this screen that can be changed from here.
sources.empty: No chain has a source configured.

leaflets.heading: Import a leaflet
leaflets.lead: Drop the JSON the extractor produced. Nothing here changes the document: an edited file has a different digest, and the digest is what stops the same leaflet being imported twice.

rejected.not-json: That file is not JSON. Check that it is the extractor's output and not the PDF.
rejected.not-a-document: That file reads as JSON but has no offers in it, so it did not come from the leaflet extractor.

read.heading: What the file says
read.chainIdHint: The chain identifier is shown and never used to look anything up. Two extractors spell one chain two ways, so pick the chain yourself below.

leaflets.scopeNeedsChain: Choose the chain first. Scopes belong to a chain, so there is nothing to choose between until there is one.
leaflets.noNational: This chain has no national scope. Most leaflets are nationwide, so create one and come back.
leaflets.createScope: Create a price scope in a new tab
leaflets.datesRequired: Both dates are needed. The file states none, or states only one, and the import is refused without both.

conflict.already-imported: This chain has already imported this exact document. Revert that run first, then import the corrected file.
conflict.run-in-progress: A run for this chain is already in progress. Only one runs at a time, so wait for it or abort it first.

failures.heading: The document was refused
failures.lead: One entry per offer, with every complaint about it. Fix the file in the extractor and drop it again: nothing on this screen edits the document.

preview.heading: What would be imported
preview.byPageAsc: Sort by page, first to last
preview.byPageDesc: Sort by page, last to first

note.loyalty: Skipped: the price on this tile is for loyalty card holders, and that is not what a shopper without the card pays.
note.conditional: Queued, not written: the printed price is the second unit's or the price at a quantity, and this tile states no single unit price.

aliases.heading: Leaflet names
aliases.empty: Every printed name for this chain has been decided.
aliases.rawText: What the extractor read on the tile

choose.body: A printed name belongs to the chain that printed it, so choose which chain to work through. The queue reads that chain's names that no leaflet could resolve.

bind.heading: Point it at a product we have
bind.candidate: A product was proposed by name. Nothing was written: agreeing here is what binds the name and writes the leaflet's price.

create.heading: Or create the product
create.help: The Spanish name starts as the leaflet printed it and can be changed freely. The English name may be left empty: the product lists with a missing translation tag and a shopper reading English sees the Spanish name. Whatever the product ends up called, the name the leaflet printed is what the next leaflet resolves against.
create.submit: Create it and bind the name

shops.heading: Source shops
shops.lead: Every shop a source names, and the shop of ours it points at. A run writes no availability for a shop nobody has mapped: it counts it and finishes.
shops.chooseChain: Choose a chain. A source's shops are only ever read one chain at a time, so there is nothing to show until you do.
shops.empty: No shop of this chain is in this state.

action.map: Map it to one of ours
action.ignore: We do not sell from here
action.unignore: Put it back in the queue

map.heading: Map this shop
map.pick: Which shop of ours is it?
map.notBackfilled: {{shop}} will point at {{location}}. This does not fill in what the last run skipped: the next run writes it.

users.noZones: This person is not in any zone.
users.zonesUnavailable: The zones could not be read. The account above is still what the server sent.

resendVerification.heading: Send the confirmation email again?
resendVerification.body: A new confirmation email goes to {{email}}, the address on {{name}}'s account. This skips the wait an ordinary resend has to sit through.

deleteAccount.heading: Delete this account?
deleteAccount.body: {{name}}'s identity is removed and their shopping lists are deleted. Any zone they own is marked for deletion, and their memberships are retired with the name they used in each zone scrubbed. What they wrote on other people's lists stays. There is no undo.

users.usernameHelp: The handle this person is known by. Changing it reaches every zone they are in: the name on each of their memberships is rewritten to match, so this is not a private label.
users.displayNameHelp: Whatever the sign in provider supplied, which for a Google account is somebody’s real full name. It is kept off every listing for that reason, and clearing it is allowed.
users.emailHelp: Fixed here. Nothing in velista changes a registered address, so there is no service to call: the four paths that write it each establish an identity, and writing the column alone would leave the credential, any linked provider and every outstanding confirmation pointing at an address the account no longer claims. Use “Resend confirmation” for an unconfirmed one.
users.emailVerifiedAtHelp: Fixed here. Setting it by hand asserts that somebody proved control of an address, which is the one thing this column exists to record and the one thing an operator cannot observe.
users.kindHelp: Fixed here. A temporary account becomes registered by upgrading, which needs a password or a linked provider and writes a credential in the same transaction; flipping the value alone would leave an account nobody can sign in to. Nothing goes the other way at all.

zones.name: Name

regenerateJoinCode.heading: Replace the join code?
regenerateJoinCode.body: {{name}} gets a new join code. Anybody holding the old one can no longer use it, including a link somebody was sent an hour ago.

deleteZone.heading: Delete this zone?
deleteZone.body: {{name}} is deleted, with its lists, its lines and everything settled inside it. Every member loses it from their app. There is no undo.

transferOwnership.heading: Hand the zone over?
transferOwnership.body: {{member}} becomes the owner of {{name}}. Whoever owns it now becomes an admin instead.

kickMember.heading: Remove this member?
kickMember.body: {{member}} loses {{name}} from their app. They can join again with the code, so ban them instead if that is not what you want.

banMember.heading: Ban this member?
banMember.body: {{member}} loses {{name}} and cannot rejoin with the code. What they already wrote on the zone's lists stays.

markForDeletion.heading: Mark this zone for deletion?
markForDeletion.body: {{name}} is put in the queue the reaper works through, and is removed for good once the grace period is up. Restoring it before then undoes this.

zones.configHelp: The zone’s own settings, as a JSON object. It is replaced whole rather than merged, which is what saving does for the zone’s owner too.
zones.ownerHelp: Fixed here. Handing the zone to somebody is “Make owner” on one of the member rows, because it is two role changes and this column in one transaction. A zone with no owner is an ordinary state, and that action is what rescues it.
zones.joinCodeHelp: Fixed here. It is unique and random on purpose, so it is minted rather than typed: “New join code” replaces it and invalidates every invitation already handed out.
zones.statusHelp: Fixed here. It is written together with “Marked for deletion” in one transaction, and the two actions below are how it moves. Writing one of the pair alone leaves a zone the reaper either never removes or removes anyway.
zones.markedForDeletionAtHelp: Fixed here, and the other half of the pair above. “Mark for deletion” sets both and “Restore” clears both.
zones.memberCountHelp: Counted from the membership below. Add or remove a member to change it.
zones.listCountHelp: Counted from the lists below. Add or remove a list to change it.

lists.name: Name
lists.zoneHelp: Fixed here. A list belongs to the zone it was made in, and nothing moves one between zones.
lists.createdByUserIdHelp: Fixed here. It records who made the list, which is a fact about what happened rather than a setting.
lists.lineCountHelp: Counted from the lines below. Add or delete a line to change it.
lists.autoApproveLinesHelp: Whether a line added from now on counts straight away. It governs new lines only, so turning it on approves nothing that is already waiting.
lists.sharedWithZoneHelp: Turning this on gives every approved member of the zone the right to read this list, write on it and decide its lines. Turning it off takes that right from nobody. It governs who arrives next, so switching it off does not close the list: to shut somebody out, remove them from the zone.

baskets.name: Name
baskets.noLines: This shopping list has no lines.
baskets.note: A shopping list is a record of what somebody took to the shop, so nothing here can be changed. It was put together from the household’s lists at a moment it remembers, and its lines carry what was claimed and settled while that person walked round. What an operator can correct is the list it came from.

admins.note: Admins are read only here, on purpose. There is no route that creates, changes or removes one, so adding an admin means running "npx nx run luna-shopper-backend-auth:admin:create" on the server, or "node admin-cli.js create <username>" inside the auth pod.

people.broadcast: Saving this is seen straight away by everybody in the zone. Somebody with the app open watches it change under their thumb, with nothing on their screen to say an operator did it.

field.idHelp: The identifier this row is addressed by. It is generated when the row is created and nothing changes it.
field.createdAtHelp: When the row was created. It records what happened and is never rewritten.

memberships.zoneIdHelp: Fixed here. A membership is one person in one zone; somebody joining a second zone gets a second membership.
memberships.userIdHelp: Fixed here. It says whose membership this is, and nothing transfers one between accounts.
memberships.usernameHelp: What this person is called inside this zone alone. Their global handle is on their account and is not touched by this.
memberships.roleHelp: Owner is deliberately not offered. Handing the zone over is “Make owner” on the zone screen, because it is two role changes and a column in one transaction.
memberships.statusHelp: Fixed here. The four actions beside this row are how it moves, because each of them does more than write this value: letting somebody in announces it to the zone, banning keeps the row so the ban survives, and refusing removes it.

approve.heading: Let this person in?
approve.body: {{name}} becomes a member of the zone and can read and write its lists straight away. The zone is told, so everybody with the app open sees them arrive.

reject.heading: Refuse this request?
reject.body: {{name}} stops waiting and the request is removed. They can ask again with the join code, so ban them instead if that is not what you want.

kick.heading: Remove this member?
kick.body: {{name}} loses the zone from their app. They can join again with the code, so ban them instead if that is not what you want.

ban.heading: Ban this member?
ban.body: {{name}} loses the zone and cannot rejoin with the code. What they already wrote on its lists stays.

lines.listIdHelp: Fixed here. A line belongs to the list it was written on, and nothing moves one between lists.
lines.approvalStatusHelp: Fixed here. The two actions beside this row are how it moves, because each is a service call that tells the zone. Correcting the wording above leaves an approved line approved.
lines.createdByUserIdHelp: Fixed here. It records who wrote the line, and an operator did not.
lines.note: There is no way to add a line here, on purpose. Every line records who wrote it, that column cannot be empty, and an operator is not a member of the household. Somebody in the zone adds a line; an operator corrects one.

approve.heading: Approve this line?
approve.body: “{{name}}” starts counting towards the shopping. Everybody in the zone sees it change.

reject.heading: Reject this line?
reject.body: “{{name}}” stops counting towards the shopping. It stays on the list, and somebody in the zone can approve it again.
